common_mistakes: Pulling only the mechanical permit and forgetting the separate electrical permit for the new disconnect
Installing the condenser before the permit is issued and posted — Seattle can stop the job and require corrections
Using the wrong electrical license or missing the WA L&I license number on the application
Failing to seal the wall penetration and support the line set properly, which can fail inspection
Submitting the permit without verifying contractor licensing/registration status before filing

pro_tips: Seattle's mechanical permit for this kind of job is relatively cheap at about $70, but the electrical permit is a separate cost — budget both up front.
Have the mini-split submittal sheet ready before you open the portal; Seattle reviewers want the exact equipment model and efficiency data.
Because Seattle is in a seismic zone, use proper mounting hardware and anchorage for the outdoor condenser and line-set supports.
Check your contractor license status before starting the application — Seattle and WA L&I will block or delay filings if the trade license is not current.
If the condenser location is tight to property lines or windows, verify setback and noise constraints before final placement.
